extracted.intended_audience: open-source investigators, journalists, and digital verification practitioners (OSINT)
extracted.subtask_description: A practical toolkit listing tools, methods and best-practices for open-source verification and digital investigation (satellite imagery, geolocation, social media, image/video forensics, archiving, infrastructure analysis, and security). It enumerates tools with pros/cons and short guidance for each investigative task.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check satellite imagery date and provenance
rubrics_metrics.description: Be able to check the date of satellite imagery and its provenance; some tools make this difficult or do not show dates clearly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The toolkit repeatedly notes difficulties (e.g. 'Difficult to check the date of the imagery' for Bing Maps). Always verify imagery dates and source (commercial vs public), and be cautious when a tool does not expose imagery timestamps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use multiple mapping and satellite sources to compare coverage and resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare Google, Bing, DigitalGlobe, Sentinel, TerraServer, Yandex and other sources to get the best coverage and highest resolution imagery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'More recent and higher resolution imagery than Google' (Bing) and 'Highest resolution available (0.3m)' (TerraServer). Add alternative imagery layers (e.g. Bing layer in Google Earth) to compare. Note differences in recency and resolution per region (e.g. Iraq, Afghanistan).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use historical imagery when available
rubrics_metrics.description: Use historical satellite or Street View imagery to compare changes over time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Google Earth Pro offers historical imagery; some tools lack historical imagery (noted as a 'Con' for certain services). Use historical layers to validate chronology of events and to detect changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Convert and normalize coordinate notation
rubrics_metrics.description: Convert geographic coordinates between different notation styles to ensure consistent geolocation references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use coordinate-conversion tools (e.g., synnatschke.de geo-tools) when sources use differing coordinate formats (decimal, DMS, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-check street-level imagery and crowdsourced photos
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Street View, Mapillary, OpenStreetCam and crowdsourced sources to corroborate ground-level visual evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pros: 'Useful addition to Google Streetview' (Mapillary). Cons: 'Little to no coverage in countries like Syria, Iraq.' Always check multiple street-level sources and be aware of coverage gaps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be aware of and document tool limitations (pros/cons, costs, OS support)
rubrics_metrics.description: Note each tool's pros/cons such as cost, resolution, coverage, platform compatibility and learning curve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The toolkit lists Pros/Cons for each entry (e.g., 'Moderate and coarse resolution imagery' or 'No native linux support'). Document these when using tools and account for limitations in reporting/investigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geobased search using platform-specific tools and operators
rubrics_metrics.description: Use geobased search tools and search operators (e.g., Twitter geocode operator) to find posts within a geographic radius.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example operator: 'geocode:[coordinates],[radius-km]' (Twitter). Use geobased search platforms (Echosec, Liveuamap, WarWire) but verify results carefully because geolocation data can be missing or faked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat geotags and geolocated posts with caution (can be faked)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that geotags and geolocated posts may be falsified; verify with on-the-ground cues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The toolkit warns 'Easy to fake.' Always corroborate with imagery, landmarks, metadata and other sources rather than trusting geotags alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reverse image search across multiple engines
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform reverse image searches (still frames, photos) using multiple engines (Google, Yandex, TinEye, Baidu) to locate prior instances and provenance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended: use several engines and plugins (RevEye). Note that some tools search a number of stills not every frame (Amnesty YouTube Dataviewer limitation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Extract and analyze metadata from images and videos
rubrics_metrics.description: Read EXIF and other metadata to gather camera, timestamp, geolocation and file history information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tools: Exiftool (command-line), Jeffrey's Image Metadata Viewer (online), Foca (Windows). Note platform constraints (e.g., no GUI for Exiftool, Windows-only tools) and that metadata can be stripped or altered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use image-forensics filters to detect manipulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply forensic analysis (error level analysis, filters) to detect doctored images or composite edits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tools: FotoForensics, Reveal Image Verification Assistant ('providing eight filters to detect still images alterations'). Document findings and remember that forensic outputs are indicators, not definitive proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use video verification plugins and document contextual data
rubrics_metrics.description: Use plugins like InVID to gather contextual data, metadata, reverse searches, forensic analysis and magnified frames for videos.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: InVID features: 'Contextual data, Metadata, reverse search (Google, Yandex, Baidu), image forensic, Magnifier.' Be aware of plugin limitations and always cite methodology when using plugin outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be aware of frame-sampling limitations in video reverse-search tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Some tools only search a number of still frames rather than every frame, which can miss evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E.g., Amnesty YouTube Dataviewer: 'Searches for a number of still, not each frame (thus results may be left out).' When frame-level analysis is critical, use tools or workflows that examine more frames or manual inspection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document exact upload times when possible
rubrics_metrics.description: Record exact upload timestamps and provenance data for videos and posts to establish chronology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use tools such as Amnesty YouTube Dataviewer for exact upload time where supported; note tool-specific caveats about what is searchable or included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Archive web pages and social content to preserve evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Use archiving services to capture and preserve webpages and social posts that may be altered or removed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tools: Archive.is, Wayback Machine. Use archivers proactively to 'Let’s you archive any webpage.' Also use site downloaders (Wayback Machine downloader) for bulk archival when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track takedown and removal history
rubrics_metrics.description: Check databases of takedown notices and DMCA complaints to understand content removal and legal context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tool: Lumen (lumendatabase.org) 'Collects and analyses legal complaints and requests for removal of online materials.' Useful to study prevalence of legal threats and the source of content removals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigate domain/DNS/IP history and infrastructure
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Passive DNS, DNS-history archives, Censys, DomainTools and related services to trace domain registration, DNS changes and server infrastructure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'PassiveDNS', 'Censys continually monitors every reachable server', 'The World's Largest Repository of historical DNS data' (DomainTools). Note API/search limits and potential costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Shodan and similar IoT search engines to investigate devices and exposed services
rubrics_metrics.description: Search for internet-connected devices, misconfigurations, and exposed services linked to an investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shodan described as 'Internet of things search engine' that 'Can find heaps of misconfigured network connected devices.' Treat results as part of infrastructure analysis; these searches 'live in the grayzone' and require caution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check geoip and network tools to contextualize server locations
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Geo IP and network diagnostic tools to approximate server locations and routing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tools: geoiptool.com, Utrace, Network-Tools. Use alongside other evidence; IP-based assertions have limitations due to proxies, CDNs, and VPNs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use company and business registries for attribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Search national and regional business registries and corporate databases to trace organizations and ownership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: OpenCorporates, EU e-Justice portal for business registries, French SIRENE dataset. Use reconciliation tools (OpenRefine) where available to match entity records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Redact potentially harmful content before viewing
rubrics_metrics.description: Remove or redact embedded potentially harmful content in documents (e.g., PDFs) before opening in your environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tools: pdf-redact-tools (GitHub). Useful to remove potentially harmful content in PDFs before viewing 'like traceback.' Follow organizational safety protocols.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use specialized tools for social media profile analysis and content downloads
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ tools that extract posts, followers, likes, and profile data for deeper analysis, with attention to limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tools: twlets (download tweets, followers and likes into Excel; 'Goes up to 3,200 tweets'), Tweetreach (reach analysis), Treeverse (visualise conversations), StalkScan, IntelTechniques. Note API limits and completeness issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use advanced search operators (Google/Twitter) to refine queries
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply platform-specific advanced operators to find content by date, site, filetype, or other constraints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Google advanced operators, Twitter advanced search, geocode operator. The toolkit references googleguide.com/advanced_operators_reference and twitter.com/search-advanced for practical use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approximate time of day using solar/shadow analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimate the time of day in imagery or photos by analyzing shadow direction and length using solar calculators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tool: SunCalc ('Make approximation of time of the day using shadow direction'). Use Wolfram|Alpha for supplementary queries. Treat approximations as ranges and corroborate with other temporal evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visualize relationships and timelines to aid analysis and presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use graph databases, timeline tools and visualization platforms to map connections and present findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tools: Neo4j (graph platform), TimelineJS (interactive timelines), DataWrapper, RAWGraphs, vis.occrp.org. Use appropriate visualization for the dataset and document methods for reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use collaborative and link-analysis tools for complex investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: Leverage collaborative platforms and link-analysis software for team investigations and complex relationship mapping.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tools: Maltego (interactive data mining and directed graphs), Montage (collaborative working), Hunch.ly, safeweb.norton.com. Note some services may be paid or closing (tool availability can change).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use unknown-hash identification when encountering unfamiliar hashes
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify the type of a hash encountered during investigation to determine next steps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tool: Unknown Hash ID (for identifying hash types so you know how to handle them during investigation). Useful when you find a hash and need to decide whether it warrants further analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enable operational security and privacy best-practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow basic security hygiene: enable two-factor authentication, use security guides, and adopt privacy-protecting services as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendations: 'Check for every digital service you use whether you have enabled two factor authentication (2FA)' and follow 'Security in a box' and Tech Solidarity basic security guides. Use privacy-focused search engines (DuckDuckGo, StartPage, Qwant) when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for tool-specific coverage gaps and geopolitical variation
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that coverage, recency and resolution vary by country and region (e.g., less coverage in Syria/Iraq for Mapillary).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many entries list region-specific pros/cons (e.g., Bing more recent in Iraq; Mapillary has little coverage in Syria). Always assess whether a tool is appropriate for your geographic area.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document and publish your methods, sources and toolchain
rubrics_metrics.description: Make investigative methods and the exact tools used explicit and reproducible when publishing findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The toolkit emphasizes guides and how-tos and mentions that methods will be highlighted with case-studies. Keep clear records of steps, pros/cons and any paid features used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be mindful of legal and ethical considerations regarding data removal and privacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Monitor takedown notices and consider privacy and legal implications when using or publishing materials obtained online.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Lumen to study takedown prevalence; follow fact-checker’s codes (Poynter) and verification handbooks. Consider removing or redacting personally identifiable information where required by ethics or law.
